paper.title_en: Bounds on nonlinear effective field theories via resurgent relative entropy
paper.abstract_en: We study a class of nonlinear effective field theories (EFTs) in which relative entropy organizes an infinite tower of higher-dimensional operators with factorially growing coefficients. Using its Borel-resummed expression, we derive bounds on EFT coefficients: under the factorial-growth ansatz, the non-negativity of relative entropy in the weak-background regime constrains the sign of their assumed asymptotic growth, while a negative real part beyond this regime signals perturbative limitations and possible sensitivity to nonperturbative effects. In fermionic QED, analytic continuation from Euclidean to Minkowski spacetime yields a controlled one-loop example: such negativity accompanies the Schwinger instability.
